subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should OpenClaw expose caller-selected `sessions_spawn` lanes with per-lane subagent concurrency config, and what lane naming/config contract should become public?
rationale: The missing source behavior is clear, but the fix adds a model-facing tool parameter and compatibility-sensitive config/default semantics that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Additive Lane Contract
options.body: Add validated `sessions_spawn.lane`, keep `subagent` as the default, forward it through native and ACP spawns, and add an explicit per-lane config shape with aggregate safety limits.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Scheduler Design
options.body: Defer this issue until maintainers settle how caller-selected lanes, per-target caps, queue visibility, and foreground per-agent lanes should share one scheduler model.

options.title: Decline Public Caller Lanes
options.body: Keep the single subagent lane and document current `maxConcurrent` constraints if model-selected lane names are not a desired public contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Additive Lane Contract
recommendation.body: Add validated `sessions_spawn.lane`, keep `subagent` as the default, forward it through native and ACP spawns, and add an explicit per-lane config shape with aggregate safety limits.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal runs through the current sessions_spawn, subagent dispatch, gateway lane setup, and config-limit code paths.
